unsupported_claims: On BlogCatalog, DeepWalk kept its advantage with as little as about 1% of nodes labeled
That is roughly 4-5 times less labeled data than the roughly 5% level at which some competitors need to match it
The named competitors (spectral clustering, modularity, EdgeCluster) are the methods DeepWalk outperforms in this setting; the evidence does not name them
rationale: The evidence supports the claim that DeepWalk does better when labels are sparse. It does not support the specific figures of 1% versus 5% or '4-5 times less data', and it does not give the 60% less training data figure, which the answer misses. The answer hedges on its numbers but still presents them as the paper's findings.
